original.target_description: Study 4: hand cleansing versus no cleansing after unethical recall; composite moral emotions including guilt, with sex as covariate and a one-tailed test.

n.sample_role: Participants in the moral-emotions analysis; exact analytic n not explicitly established.
n.location: p. 1451, Table 1; p. 1452, moral-emotions paragraph and note 12

replication.target_description: Fayard et al. (2009), Study 2: main effect of hand wipe on self-reported moral emotions following unethical recall, in a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects ANOVA including scent and hand rubbing.

n.location: p. 25, Study 2, Participants; p. 26, Results and Discussion
n.quote: Participants consisted of 119 undergraduates from Kwantlen Polytechnic University who participated in exchange for partial course credit in psychology courses. Four participants’ data could not be used due to their failure to comply with the experimental procedure.
n.sample_role: Undergraduate participants; 119 is recruited sample, not a printed final analytic total for the moral-emotion test.
n.exclusions: Four excluded for procedural noncompliance: own antiseptic cream, premature wipe use, refusal to use wipe, or no unethical story. Final analytic total is not explicitly printed.

es.location: p. 26 (PDF p. 6), Study 2, Results and Discussion
es.quote: Regarding the reduction of moral emotions, ANOVA revealed no significant main effects for hand wipe F (1, 107) = .01, p = .93, ηp2 = .00, nor for the added conditions.

p.location: p. 26 (PDF p. 6), Study 2, Results and Discussion
p.quote: Regarding the reduction of moral emotions, ANOVA revealed no significant main effects for hand wipe F (1, 107) = .01, p = .93, ηp2 = .00, nor for the added conditions.

reported_success.quote: In terms of the effect of hand washing on moral emotions and altruistic behavior, Study 2 also failed to replicate Zhong and Liljenquist’s (2006) results.
